title: The 5 Best Car Seats Under $300
metaDescription: Our 5 picks for car seats under $300, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at car seats under $300 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Graco 4Ever DLX 4-in-1 Car Seat
products.blurb: Key specs: 4-in-1: rear-facing, forward-facing, highback booster, backless booster, Rear-facing 4 to 40 pounds, forward-facing 22 to 65 pounds, 10-year usable lifespan.
strengths: Covers newborn through booster years in a single seat, the widest span in this budget
limitations: Bulkier footprint than a dedicated infant seat, less ideal for daily carrying
Booster-stage capacity is unused for the first several years of ownership
features: 4-in-1: rear-facing, forward-facing, highback booster, backless booster
Rear-facing 4 to 40 pounds, forward-facing 22 to 65 pounds
Simply Safe Adjust harness with integrated buckle lock-off
Typically $280 to $320, often on sale within this budget

products.name: Chicco KeyFit 35 Infant Car Seat
products.blurb: Key specs: Fits infants 4 to 35 pounds, Stay-in-car base with load leg and level indicator, Removable infant head and body support insert.
strengths: One of the best-reviewed infant seats for install accuracy on the first attempt
Wide stroller compatibility makes it a practical travel-system anchor
limitations: Only covers the infant stage, a convertible seat purchase still lies ahead
Height limit around 30 inches means an earlier switch than some competitors
A second base for a two-car household adds to the total spend within this budget
features: Stay-in-car base with load leg and level indicator
Removable infant head and body support insert

products.name: Evenflo LiteMax 35 Infant Car Seat
products.blurb: Key specs: Fits infants 4 to 35 pounds, 8.7-pound carrier shell, Belt lock-off for base-free installation.
strengths: Lightest carrier of the three, easier for daily lifting
Meets the same federal safety standard as the pricier picks in this list
limitations: Fewer premium features than the KeyFit 35 or 4Ever DLX
Only covers the infant stage, same limitation as the KeyFit 35
Fabric and padding feel noticeably less premium than the pricier picks
features: Leaves the most remaining budget of the three picks here

products.name: Graco Extend2Fit Convertible Car Seat
strengths: Rear-facing to 50 lb, forward-facing harness to 65 lb
Extension panel lets kids stay rear-facing longer
No-rethread harness adjusts with the headrest
InRight LATCH connectors for quick installation
limitations: Takes more front-to-back room when the extension is used
